0|dab4e1f06cabb6834de14264394ccab197007302|torvalds~linux|/home/usuario01/Titan-Files-Research/src/_00/output/C/torvalds~linux|False|"bpf: Derive source IP addr via bpf_*_fib_lookup()
Extend the bpf_fib_lookup() helper by making it to return the source
IPv4/IPv6 address if the BPF_FIB_LOOKUP_SRC flag is set.
For example
column2: the following snippet can be used to derive the desired

column1: source IP address:
struct bpf_fib_lookup p = { .ipv4_dst = ip4->daddr };
ret = bpf_skb_fib_lookup(skb
BPF_FIB_LOOKUP_SRC | BPF_FIB_LOOKUP_SKIP_NEIGH);
if (ret != BPF_FIB_LKUP_RET_SUCCESS)
return TC_ACT_SHOT;
/* the p.ipv4_src now contains the source address */
The inability to derive the proper source address may cause malfunctions
in BPF-based dataplanes for hosts containing netdevs with more than one
routable IP address or for multi-homed hosts.
For example
column2: Cilium implements packet masquerading in BPF. If an

column1: egressing netdev to which the Cilium's BPF prog is attached has
multiple IP addresses
column2: then only one [hardcoded] IP address can be used for

column1: masquerading. This breaks connectivity if any other IP address should have
been selected instead
column3: when a public and private addresses

column1: are attached to the same egress interface.
The change was tested with Cilium [1].
Nikolay Aleksandrov helped to figure out the IPv6 addr selection.
